statements.status_notes: OpenTelemetry API 1.62.0 removes io.opentelemetry.common.impl.ApiUsageLogger, which Elasticsearch's APM tracer depends on. Upgrading causes NoClassDefFoundError at runtime. The fix requires upstream Elasticsearch code changes to support the newer OpenTelemetry API. The vulnerability affects W3C baggage propagation with unbounded memory allocation, but most Java HTTP servers enforce 8 KiB header limits by default, mitigating external attack vectors.

Jackson Core 2.19.2 is embedded in parquet-hadoop-bundle-1.17.0.jar (shaded dependency in esql-datasource-iceberg and esql-datasource-parquet modules), and Jackson Core 2.17.2 is embedded in elasticsearch-x-content-9.4.1.jar. These are shaded/relocated dependencies that cannot be bumped via Gradle resolutionStrategy. Fixing requires either upstream Elasticsearch to rebuild these modules with patched Jackson versions, or bumping to parquet-hadoop-bundle versions that embed fixed Jackson (if available). The vulnerability allows unbounded memory allocation via crafted JSON, but Elasticsearch's typical deployment behind reverse proxies with request size limits provides some mitigation.

Bouncy Castle BC-FIPS 2.1.0-2.1.2 has an inconsistency in AVX/AVX-512f GCM pipelines (gcm128w, gcm512w) on x86_64 Linux. No upstream fix is available; Maven Central publishes no release beyond 2.1.2. The vulnerability has local attack vector (CVSS AV:L) with availability-only impact (CVSS VA:L). Monitoring upstream for a patched release.

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
